target_customer: Devops and security teams running Linux servers who need to know which new vulnerabilities affect their own installed packages
problem: Teams are flooded with vulnerability advisories and patch late. Patchwork notified users only about vulnerable packages actually installed on their machines, aiming to cut the time between a fix and patched infrastructure to zero.
business_model: SaaS billed per machine (pricing still undecided at launch per the Show HN thread)
product_category: Developer security, vulnerability and patch notification

founders.name: Shamiq Islam
prior_employers: Matasano (stated in the Show HN post as ex-Matasano)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the founder.

founders.name: David (surname not found)
founders.background_notes: Posts as dchanm in the Show HN thread and says he worked on AppSec at Mozilla when Shellshock came out. Not named on the YC page.

competitors.name: appCanary
competitors.what: Real time notifications about whether a company's infrastructure is vulnerable, a YC S15 company

competitors.name: Pakiti
competitors.what: Open source tool that checks which patches are missing on servers, cited by a Show HN commenter as useful in this space

competitors.name: Nexpose (Rapid7)
competitors.what: Commercial vulnerability scanner that a commenter wanted Patchwork to integrate with

technical_complexity.rationale: Scraping vulnerability feeds, matching them to package inventories reported by agents and notifying users was standard engineering with a tricky data matching problem; the founders had security backgrounds.

defensibility.rationale: The data came from public upstream announcements and the agent was a simple shell script, so copying took weeks and appCanary already offered similar alerts.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying is documented. The domain now redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page, and no shutdown statement was found.

market_need_then: The Shellshock disclosure in 2014 raised awareness of patch latency, as the co-founder noted in the Show HN thread, which drew 122 points and 50 comments per a search result. No spend figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Used patchworksecurity.com (descriptive compound with 'security'), which now redirects to a domain for sale page (observed on fetch).
branding.community_and_virality: A Show HN launch post about 'Patchwork' drew 122 points and 50 comments (search result), the only brand level attention found.

brand_strength.rationale: Only a Show HN launch discussion exists; the name collides with unrelated companies called Patchwork or Patchstack and left no lasting brand.

outcome_analysis: Why Patchwork Security went inactive is not public. A two person team launched on Hacker News with a narrow apt based product against appCanary and open source tools, and no later round, shutdown post or acquisition was found. The domain is now for sale. With no sourced cause, failure factors stay empty.
notes: The seed round is recorded from a Crunchbase listing that shows Y Combinator as lead but no amount or date; this rests on a single database. A StartupIntros April 2024 seed for 'Patchwork' was rejected as a different company. The Show HN page gave only a relative date, so competitor dates are approximate (as_of 2016-01 is inferred from the W16 batch). appCanary's page was seen in a search result and not opened; its date is the S15 batch year. The company site redirected to a GoDaddy sale page and I did not follow it. Pakiti and Nexpose dates are set to 2016-01 from the Show HN launch thread, whose page showed only a relative date; this is approximate.
